files.title: Deployment and recovery
files.description: CPU hosting, isolated PostgreSQL, encrypted snapshots and incident recovery.
files.context:
## Current deployment and data

Noteweld runs its Next.js/Node application on Modal behind the public Cloudflare gateway. Neon PostgreSQL stores private account/note state. The preview has explicit account/note/source bounds and billing is closed. No shared wallet/login across the portfolio apps is implied.

## Account and preference persistence

Every private operation validates the server session and owner. Browser-session revocation and account session versions control continuing access. Google/GitHub entry is configured, with actual owner grant/link acceptance still pending; matching emails never automatically merge accounts. Verified email signup and mailed recovery are deployed and passed real inbox checks. Existing key/provider recovery is preserved; accounts never silently merge.

Guest appearance is browser-local. Saved account appearance is stored with the account and included in exports/backups. Local drafts are not a crash-proof offline database. The owner's private code map and learning material are not public app features.

## Backups and migrations

The November preferences release took a fresh encrypted snapshot before its additive migration. Account/note/provider-identity counts were preserved. Current snapshot format 6 includes appearance, billing and media metadata; media bytes have separate private storage copies. The email/storage releases use schema 0011. Fresh encrypted pre/post snapshots restored with original durable data preserved. Pending inbox challenges and active browser sessions are excluded, and restored sessions are invalidated. Restore targets must be empty and isolated, and restored sessions must be invalidated. A local backup file alone does not prove off-device disaster recovery.

Owner deployment, credential and recovery commands remain in the access-controlled repository. Keep application public-origin settings and gateway forwarding behavior consistent during rollback. Never erase accounts, identities or quotas to make a deployment appear healthy.

## Verification scope

A successful build is distinct from browser review, database persistence and real provider consent. The deployed release passed ordinary email sign-in, note save, account appearance save/reload/export and temporary-account deletion; [the current release](/manuals/noteweld/ui-release/) gives the relevant counts and limits.

[Using Noteweld](/manuals/noteweld/guide/) explains normal operation; [public domain access](/manuals/noteweld/custom-domain/) explains the hosting boundary.

## Attachments and storage

Managed images/audio/video live in private R2 storage. [Storage and plans](/manuals/noteweld/storage/) explains the 100 MB free allowance, reserved/unfinished bytes, downloads, deletion and safe over-limit behavior. Paid access remains disabled; sandbox exercises are not real payments. Private operating budgets, credentials and owner code maps are omitted.

files.title: Custom domain and account access
files.description: Public hostname, secure gateway, existing-account access and rollback.
files.context:
## Current public address

Use **https://noteweld.amirgomaa.com/**. The account-free editor and graph are `/example` and `/example/graph`; private writing starts at `/auth/signin`. The application runs on Modal behind a fixed Cloudflare HTTPS gateway, with PostgreSQL on Neon. Vercel is not its active host.

Existing account data stays in the same independent database. Sign in again when changing hostnames; browser cookies and guest local storage do not automatically move between website origins. Matching email addresses do not merge accounts.

## Public origin and authentication

The deployed Auth.js base URL is the public Noteweld origin. The gateway preserves validated public Origin/Referer values and supplies the fixed public forwarded host while fetching the fixed Modal upstream. Foreign unsafe origins are rejected before forwarding; private responses stream without shared caching. The November release repaired the older internal-origin mapping that blocked account writes after OAuth activation.

Google/GitHub authorization redirects use the registered public callbacks, state/PKCE and Google nonce. Real owner consent/link acceptance remains a separate step. [Account controls](/manuals/noteweld/account-work/) explain deliberate linking and recovery.

## Recovery boundary

Preserve the public-origin contract when changing deployment versions: rolling back only the gateway to its old internal-origin mapping would break writes. Keep accounts, identities, backups and credentials intact. An additive UI/preferences rollback does not require deleting data.

[Using Noteweld](/manuals/noteweld/guide/) is the visitor starting point; [the interface release](/manuals/noteweld/ui-release/) records current verification.

files.title: Accounts, recovery and connected sign-in
files.description: Current email/private-key recovery, browser sessions and deliberately linked Google/GitHub identities.
files.context:
## Sign in and retain recovery access

Create an email account by completing the security check, following the inbox link and explicitly choosing your name/passphrase. Verified email/password accounts can request mailed resets; links expire after 30 minutes and work once. A completed reset signs out previous sessions and invalidates any old private recovery key. Existing unverified accounts retain their previous key/provider recovery. Configured Google/GitHub sign-in remains a separate method; accounts never silently merge. Each portfolio application has a separate account.

## Link a provider to an existing account

Sign in to the existing Noteweld account first. Open **Account → Sessions and connected sign-in → Provider identities**. Confirm ownership when asked, then choose **Link Google** or **Link GitHub**. Sensitive actions require ownership confirmation from the last five minutes. If it has expired, choosing an action explains the requirement and focuses the confirmation field; it does not change an identity. Enter the current passphrase or choose the private recovery key, confirm ownership, then choose the action again. Matching email addresses never silently merge accounts.

Google/GitHub registrations and public-domain authorization requests have passed callback, state and PKCE checks; Google also uses an OIDC nonce. The owner's actual consent/link/unlink acceptance remains pending. A configured button is not evidence of a completed provider grant.

## Sessions, copies and deletion

Review active browser sessions, revoke a selected device or sign out every device. Export important notes/account data before deletion. Changing a passphrase or using recovery rotates recovery access and revokes older sessions. Removing a provider must leave a usable sign-in method.

[Start with the current usage guide](/manuals/noteweld/guide/) or read [the November release](/manuals/noteweld/ui-release/).

files.title: Interface and appearance release — 5 November
files.description: Approved interface/logo, complete color preferences, saved account settings and concrete release evidence.
files.context:
## What is live

The approved forest interface and custom joined-note N logo are deployed. Open **Appearance** in the signed-in sidebar, or [try browser-only appearance settings](https://noteweld.amirgomaa.com/appearance).

Choose Forest, Paper, Slate, Graphite, Ocean or Rose; light, dark or system mode; and customize 29 semantic color roles. Light and dark retain separate overrides. Text size, reading font, spacing, reduced motion, stronger borders, individual/full reset and validated theme JSON import/export are available.

Guest choices save in that browser. Signed-in choices save to the account and are included in account exports and backups. Preview changes are explicit; choose **Save preferences** to keep them. Low-contrast colors produce a warning, with an optional repair action that preserves the user's ability to choose.

## What was checked

The release passed 58 unit/UI cases, 33 real PostgreSQL cases and 24 browser journeys; two optional locally unconfigured provider cases were skipped. Seven rendered app states had no automated WCAG A/AA/2.1 AA findings. Desktop/mobile captures and a fresh design review were completed.

Actual public-domain email sign-in, a note save, account appearance save/reload/export and temporary-account deletion passed. An encrypted backup preceded the additive preference migration; existing account/note/provider-identity counts were preserved. The gateway/public-origin mismatch discovered by live testing was repaired without weakening foreign-origin rejection.

Google/GitHub authorization requests use the registered public callbacks with state/PKCE and Google nonce; actual owner consent/link acceptance remains pending. Chromium and automated checks do not establish universal browser/accessibility coverage or perfect custom-palette contrast. Billing remains closed.

[Using Noteweld](/manuals/noteweld/guide/) explains the supported workflow.

files.title: Google and GitHub status
files.description: Configured providers, explicit linking, recovery and the remaining real-consent acceptance step.
files.context:
## Configuration and actual use are different checks

Google and GitHub are configured for Noteweld's public domain. Authorization request checks passed the exact callback URL, state and PKCE; Google also includes its OIDC nonce. Ordinary email sign-in and authenticated note/account operations passed the deployed release checks.

The owner's actual provider consent, linking/unlinking, cancellation and provider-specific email cases have not yet completed acceptance. Do not interpret configuration as evidence that every external account has been exercised.

## Existing account? Link deliberately

First sign in using the method that already owns your notes. Then open **Account → Sessions and connected sign-in → Provider identities**, confirm ownership if asked and choose the desired provider. If ownership confirmation has expired, the action remains clickable and guides you to the confirmation field. Confirm using your passphrase or private recovery key and retry the action. Google linking requests an explicit account choice. Matching email addresses do not automatically combine accounts.

[Account controls and recovery](/manuals/noteweld/account-work/) describe the supported safety controls. The [usage guide](/manuals/noteweld/guide/) is the normal starting point.

files.title: Email signup and password recovery
files.description: Verified signup, one-use inbox links, password resets and legacy recovery.
files.context:
## Create an email account

Open [signup](https://noteweld.amirgomaa.com/auth/signup), complete the security check and request your email. Follow the link, choose your name and passphrase, then confirm. Opening the link alone creates no account. Links expire after 30 minutes and work once. Use at least 15 characters, following the form's full password requirements.

## Recover access

Verified email/password accounts can [request a reset](https://noteweld.amirgomaa.com/auth/forgot). Completing the emailed form changes the password and signs out previous sessions. Any old private recovery key stops working. Unverified legacy accounts retain their existing key/provider methods; inbox ownership never silently merges or takes over an older account.

## What was checked

The owner completed actual security widgets in Firefox. Signup and reset messages reached the inbox; explicit confirmation, reused-link refusal, old-session/password rejection, replacement login and temporary-account deletion passed. Local suites cover additional expiry, concurrency and provider-failure boundaries. Separate raw widget-token replay was not captured. Google/GitHub consent remains a separate acceptance task.

[Using Noteweld](/manuals/noteweld/guide/) covers the normal workspace. Private anti-abuse budgets and provider credentials are not published.

files.title: Images, audio and video
files.description: Attach, preview, retain, download and delete private note media.
files.context:
## Add a file to a note

Choose **Attach media**, paste or drop one supported file into the editor attachment area. Save the note after insertion. Preview shows supported images and native audio/video players; codec support depends on the browser.

Images can be up to 10 MB and audio/video up to 25 MB per file. The free account allowance is 100 MB, with at most 500 attachments. Ready files live in private Cloudflare R2 storage with a recovery copy; account permissions control reads. Notes and media are not end-to-end encrypted.

## Keep or remove files

Open **Account → Manage storage and plan → Manage stored attachments** to download or remove a file. Removing only its Markdown reference keeps the reusable original in the library. Deleting the library file affects every note using it. Download anything important first.

Account JSON includes an attachment manifest, not the actual media bytes; download those separately. Archived/trashed notes and unfinished reservations still count. Shared availability can temporarily pause uploads without disclosing private accounting.

## Evidence

Actual public HTTPS checks passed original-byte storage/recovery, private access and foreign-account refusal, ranges, native image/audio/video playback, saved-note reload, invalid/oversize rejection and explicit deletion. This does not certify every browser codec or an unlimited hosting allowance.

[Storage and plan behavior](/manuals/noteweld/storage/) explains usage and over-limit recovery.

files.title: Storage usage and plans
files.description: Usage, reserved bytes, file management, planned Plus and safe downgrade.
files.context:
## Find your usage

Open [Account → Manage storage and plan](https://noteweld.amirgomaa.com/dashboard/account#storage). The panel shows saved files, unfinished uploads, pending removals and remaining space. Free includes 100 MB and at most 500 attachments; images can be up to 10 MB, audio/video up to 25 MB each.

Reservations and unfinished removals count until released. Archived/trashed notes still count. Expand the library to download ready files or remove an unneeded file/reservation. Removal warns that any note using the file will show an unavailable attachment. Refresh retries a failed read; stale displayed values are labeled.

## More storage and changes of plan

Plus is planned at $5/month for 5 GB. Subscriptions are not available yet; no payment or production upgrade is implied by a local sandbox test.

When files exceed the current allowance, new uploads pause. Notes, existing-file downloads and deletion remain available. Plan expiry does not automatically delete saved files. Account JSON contains a manifest, so download media separately for a complete copy.

## Verification

Unit and actual isolated database tests cover charged reservations, current-plan admission, local sandbox Plus, expiry and retained read/delete access. Browser checks cover local download/removal/reclaimed quota, failure/retry, themes and separately mocked full/unavailable states. Independent review approved the local interface. The deployed account screen and quota metadata passed a documented temporary operator-session check; its session was removed. Encrypted pre/post snapshots restored with original durable data unchanged. Real commercial billing remains a separate gate.

[Using Noteweld](/manuals/noteweld/guide/) is the normal starting point. Private operating budgets, credentials and internal admission configuration are omitted.

files.title: Subscription availability
files.description: Planned storage subscriptions and the distinction between test and real payments.
files.context:
## Current availability

Subscriptions and live checkout remain disabled. The current free preview includes 100 MB of managed media. Plus is planned at $5/month for 5 GB; planned capacity is not an active purchase offer.

## Preparation is not a real payment

Paddle sandbox server preparation and isolated tests cover protected checkout intents, signed-event validation, duplicates, ordered state, reconciliation and owner boundaries. Local sandbox Plus storage tests never grant production storage or prove an actual purchase.

Merchant approval, actual sandbox checkout delivery, commercial capacity, live activation and payment/payout acceptance remain separate. The interface must not take a payment while checkout is unavailable.

[Storage and plans](/manuals/noteweld/storage/) describes today's limits and safe over-limit behavior. Owner verification documents, provider credentials and private operating budgets are excluded from this public edition.

files.title: Owner operations
files.description: Usage reporting, admission controls, pause, encrypted ledger backups and recovery.
files.context:
## Current public operating boundary

Pageweft runs behind its public Cloudflare gateway on Modal. Email/passphrase and private-key recovery are deployed. Accounts and balances are product-specific. Google and mailed password reset remain unconfigured; paid checkout is closed.

## Admission and privacy

Live free processing checks visitor eligibility and private shared availability before dispatch. An unavailable or unverifiable admission check refuses new processing with **Currently unavailable. Please try again later.** Completed examples remain open. Signing in does not reset sample eligibility.

Owner accounting amounts, spending settings, usage, reset details and private reports are deliberately omitted from public documentation and responses. Customer quotes and balances are a separate contract. An admission estimate is not proof of actual provider charges or a physically isolated provider billing account.

## Durable work and recovery

The application records processing state and accounting transactionally, separates source/derived material, and checks ownership before private downloads. Retries and partial failures have explicit state and settlement behavior. Download retained outputs before their normal 48-hour expiry; immediate deletion closes access and removes supported files while financial records remain separate.

Owner pause, diagnostics, backup and recovery commands are private operational tools. They are not public administration routes. Preserve source/ledger ownership, idempotency and admission gates during recovery; do not reset quotas or disable guards to reopen a trial.

## Payment and quality evidence

The owner reports domain approval; seller/payout readiness and genuine payment/refund/payout acceptance remain separate. No billing activation or provider account change was performed by this guide refresh. Representative OCR/transcription quality, scale and margins require their own evidence.

[Use the application](/manuals/pageweft/guide/) or read [current provider boundaries](/manuals/journal/provider-costs-and-payments/).

The completed PDF example, public guide, private email account/recovery flow and bounded processing interface are deployed. Live sample availability is checked privately and may temporarily close; an example remains useful without another processing job.

## What is still gated

Paid processing packs remain closed. App-domain approval is owner-reported; actual seller/payout readiness and genuine payment/refund/payout acceptance still require their own evidence. Do not infer merchant readiness from a successful processing demo or mocked payment tests.

Current scope, retention, extraction routes and review controls are in [Using Pageweft](/manuals/pageweft/guide/). Source inspection and error flags do not certify OCR fidelity. A complete synthetic text-only book is not a representative difficult-book OCR benchmark.

## Owner controls stay private

Guest accounting amounts, provider usage, reset details and private reports are not part of the visitor contract. Availability can close when eligibility or safety evidence is unavailable. Customer processing quotes remain a separate contract.

[Provider boundaries](/manuals/journal/provider-costs-and-payments/) distinguish deployed product functions from remaining commercial acceptance.

files.title: The scientific recording example
files.description: A credited human-voiced NOAA interview excerpt, original recognition and clearly labeled editorial notes.
files.context:
## Listen to a real scientific explanation

The completed Sonaweft example is a continuous **63.65-second NOAA Ocean Podcast excerpt** about why gravity varies across Earth. Megan Forbes interviews physicist Derek van Westrum in [Understanding Gravity, episode 33](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/podcast/mar20/gravity.html). The selected passage runs from 181.05 to 244.70 seconds in the source episode.

The example credits NOAA and the speakers, links the original source and states that no endorsement is implied. It is third-party source material, not an original recording made for this portfolio. The excerpt contains speech rather than a music insert; the reuse review is specific to this selected source.

## What you are seeing

The saved transcript comes from actual Whisper recognition. Recognition, manual corrections, source attribution and editorial listening notes remain separate. The listening notes are explicitly labeled as prepared with AI assistance; they are not output from Sonaweft's optional review provider. No new processing job is needed to open the example.

Listen, follow timestamps, try the review controls and download the complete bundle. Source offsets and hashes preserve traceability; a good short example does not certify transcription accuracy on every recording.

[Hear the completed example](https://sonaweft.amirgomaa.com/example) or follow [the usage guide](/manuals/sonaweft/guide/).
